newsitem.title: GERMANY: German June industrial output up 1.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: German June industrial output up 1.4 percent.

text.p: German industrial production rose 1.4 percent in June from May, the Economics Ministry said Monday, in line with economists' expectations.

Private-sector analysts said the data were consistent with forecasts of a 2 to 2.5 percent economic expansion this year and could leave room for the Bundesbank to nudge interest rates higher soon if the mark continues to weaken.
The ministry said the preliminary data were likely to be revised up substantially. Figures for May were revised sharply downward to show a 1.5 percent fall.

"With record low interest rates, we can see that the Bundesbank has stimulated the economy extraordinarily, and if the dollar remains strong it will have to rethink its position," said economist Holger Schmieding at Merrill Lynch in Frankfurt.
"If the dollar goes over 1.87 marks, it could raise rates this month, and if not, it could wait until September or October," Schmieding said.
No sooner were those words spoken than the dollar resumed its rise in midday European trading, hitting 1.8717 marks, its highest level since October 1989.

Robert Prior-Wandesforde at HSBC James Capel in London said he sees no risk of the weak mark generating inflation, but that the Bundesbank might move on interest rates to defend the mark if it nears 1.90 to the U.S. dollar.

"I don't think there's any inflationary threat out there and the domestic side of the economy is very flat ... They may well do something if the mark continues to fall at this rate. But I don't think it will serve to turn the currency around."
Leading the upturn in June output were construction, with output up 6 percent, and consumer durables, with up 5.2 percent, the data showed.

Output rose in western and eastern Germany rose more slowly than the national figure because of differences in statistical methods. Production in western Germany rose by 0.4 percent in June, and by 0.5 percent in the east.
On a two-month basis, output in Germany was up by 0.9 percent in May and June compared with the same period a year earlier.
Over the first half of 1997, industrial production was 2.3 percent higher than a year earlier. In western Germany it was up by 1.8 percent and in the east by 3.9 percent.
